title: How Can You Use Inito in Your Follicular Phase?
summary: Learn how to use Inito in your follicular phase to identify your fertile window, track hormone changes, log fertility data, and better understand your cycle.
body_markdown:
## Why should you track your LH surge?


LH rises shortly before ovulation and typically signals that **ovulation is likely within the next 24-36 hours.**


Identifying this surge helps narrow down your most fertile days and can improve timing for intercourse or insemination. However, LH patterns are often more complex than many people realize. Research shows that not everyone experiences a single sharp surge. Approximately[48% of women have one distinct LH surge](https://www.fertstert.org/article/S0015-0282(12)02135-8/fulltext) , while others experience other types of LH surge patterns, like plateau surges, biphasic surges, or multiple LH rises[before ovulation](https://blog.inito.com/lh-surge-and-ovulation/) .


**Know more:**[What Does a Normal LH Level Look Like?](https://blog.inito.com/normal-lh-level/)


Additionally, LH concentrations during a surge vary widely between individuals. In one study, ovulation occurred across a broad range of LH values–from around[6.5 mIU/mL to over 100 mIU/mL](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272175944_Development_of_the_first_urinary_reproductive_hormone_ranges_referenced_to_independently_determined_ovulation_day) –meaning there is no “universal” threshold that applies to everyone.


However, traditional ovulation predictor kits often rely on population averages and commonly detect alpha-LH, which may be more susceptible to cross-reactivity. Inito measures beta-LH and gives you results based on your unique baseline, providing a more personalized picture of your LH pattern and cycle trends. **Know more:**[How Accurate Are Ovulation Tests?](https://blog.inito.com/how-accurate-are-ovulation-tests/)
